newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: WTO head urges open markets in S.Korea.
newsitem.headline: WTO head urges open markets in S.Korea.

text.p: South Korea should not let concerns about its current account deficit undermine its commitment to free trade, the director-general of the World Trade Organisation said on Wednesday.

"Korea has to remain an open country, and everything that Korea has to do in taking care of its problem of the current account deficit (should) not touch the principles of free trade," Renato Ruggiero told Reuters in an interview.

South Korea's current account deficit has been forecast at $18 billion this year, down from a record $23.72 billion in 1996. Economic growth has slowed, but is still expected to reach 5-6 percent this year.
Ruggiero said six percent growth would be considered a "tremendous achievement" by South Korea's major trading partners and that South Korea's basic economy appears strong.
Ruggiero met with President Kim Young-sam and the finance and trade ministers on Wednesday.

He was reluctant to reveal the substance of Wednesday's meetings, but said Korean officials insisted the government was not involved in an ongoing frugality campaign that has angered Korea's trading partners.

"What they would like is certainly to give a very strong signal that they are not involved in the frugality campaign. (That) they are involved in correcting the current account deficit through macroeconomic measures," Ruggiero said.
The South Korean government last summer mounted an austerity campaign and asked Koreans to reduce unnecessary spending.
While the government was careful not to single out imports in that campaign it has done so in the past. Some consumer groups have openly urged Koreans not to buy imports.
Ruggiero said the Korean government had expressed a "firm intention" not to violate its free-trade obligations under the WTO.
He said neither the United States nor the European Union have made formal complaints to the WTO about Korea's frugality campaign.
"There are concerns which have been publicly expressed by a number of member countries but for the moment, no more than that," he said.
Ruggiero was scheduled to meet the foreign minister and business leaders on Thursday before leaving for China on Friday where discussions will center on China's entry to the WTO.
